title: Dispatch LTP 1: Tomorrow’s Chronicle Arrives Before Dawn
summary: A bundle delivered to the press bears a date that has not yet come.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The Alderwick Chronicle received forty copies of its own newspaper at 5:10 this morning. They bear tomorrow’s date, 3 September, and include articles no member of the staff has written. The bundle was tied with our customary blue cord and left beside the pressroom door while the night watchman was inside.

The leading report describes a crane breaking at the south dock shortly after noon tomorrow. It names the foreman and records the loss of three crates of glass. The foreman has since confirmed that those crates are due to be lifted. The crane has passed its morning inspection.

Editor Julian Ashcombe ordered the bundle secured and sent copies to the police, the dock authority, and Dr. Lenora Saye of the Eidetical Institute. He has declined to print the article in today’s edition. “If this is a warning, those who can act have it,” he said. “If it is a deception, we need not carry it into every home in Alderwick.”

The pages otherwise resemble an ordinary issue. They contain a theatre notice, yesterday’s market prices, and a report credited to this correspondent on a council meeting that has not yet occurred. Its account includes a motion we had not been told would be proposed.

One difference troubled the compositors. In the future issue, our printer’s mark appears slightly out of line, as it does when a particular piece of type wears thin. The piece is in its case today and has not yet been set for tomorrow’s run.
